claims.text: The initial coating system consists of elemental Cr deposited directly on zirconium-alloy fuel cladding.
A 50–200 nm CrN interlayer is to be deposited at the Cr/zirconium-alloy interface.
The CrN interlayer will be dense and well adhered.
CrN has a high melting point and low atomic diffusivity.
The refractory nature and low diffusivity of CrN will make the interlayer a physical and chemical diffusion barrier.
The CrN interlayer will significantly slow Cr–Zr interdiffusion during high-temperature exposure.
Slowing Cr–Zr interdiffusion will suppress deleterious intermetallic phases or diffusion-induced weaknesses.
Suppressing intermetallic formation and diffusion-induced weaknesses will preserve the integrity of the protective Cr coating and prevent premature failure.
Normal-operation performance is evaluated in subcritical water at approximately 300–350°C.
Accident performance is evaluated in high-temperature steam at 900–1000°C for exposure durations on the order of minutes.
Relative to a directly Cr-coated baseline, the CrN-containing system will exhibit markedly reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion after accident-relevant steam exposure.
Relative to the baseline, the CrN-containing system will exhibit superior coating integrity after accident-relevant steam exposure.
The CrN-containing system will maintain performance comparable to the baseline under normal subcritical-water conditions.
A 900°C, 10-minute high-temperature-steam exposure can discriminate the interdiffusion and integrity performance of the CrN-modified system from the baseline.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant reduction in Cr–Zr interdiffusion, or observation of similar or worse diffusion and coating degradation, would falsify the proposed protective effect.
